newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch up, seen up slightly on Wed.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch up, seen up slightly on Wed.

text.p: Polish shares inched up after a four-session dip and analysts said the bourse's recent 38 percent bull run in which large-cap stocks surged had led to a relatively flat market in which small-cap stocks thrived.

They said the main market should rise slightly again on Wednesday, fuelled by more large speculative rises by small-cap fundamentally less sound firms, and that a deeper profit-taking correction could soon hit.
"It looks like the end of the growth phase because... fundamentally weak firms are starting to grow strongly," said Ryszard Sikora of Bank Slaski brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.2 percent to 18,122.0 points and turnover rose 17.8 percent to 195.3 million zlotys on all three markets.
None of the main market's eight top gainers on Tuesday make up more than 0.5 percent of the WIG index.
Bank Komunalny rose the daily maximum 10 percent and Irena 9.6 percent in moderate trade.
Espebepe rose 9.5 percent and did not trade after price fixing due to excess demand, with some investors possibly speculating before the firm's creditors meet on March 14, analysts said.
Post-price-fixing buying of Remak and Swarzedz, both up 9.4 percent, was strong enough for investors to have their bids reduced.

NFI units jumped 4.8 percent to 175 zlotys in 65.4-million-zloty trade in the bourse's regular session, buoyed by recent foreign analysts appraisals of the units at 240 zlotys and higher, analysts said.
The units fell 0.6 percent to 176 zlotys in 77.1-million-zloty continuous trade, where most stocks rose and turnover was at 19.8 million zlotys.
